prompt.provenance_instruction: Answer the following question about Drosophila neuroscience. For every claim you make, state where the information comes from - for example: the specific database, dataset, or tool query you used; the publication (with full citation); or your general training knowledge. If you are uncertain or do not have a source, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The calyx is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: There are several types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain, including [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are projection neurons from the antennal lobe and sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx. VFB records show [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, including larval uniglomerular projection neurons and larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons. The connectome data indicates [601](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body. VFB holds [27619](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, but this query has not been run yet.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to various brain regions through neurons with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals. VFB records show [266](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in antennal lobe") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the antennal lobe, including adult olfactory receptor neurons and larval antennal lobe local neurons. The connectome data indicates [518](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in antennal lobe") neurons with postsynaptic terminals in the antennal lobe, such as adult antennal lobe projection neurons and adult multiglomerular antennal lobe projection neurons.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
Approximately more than 125,000 neurons.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions including navigation/orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal or memory-related behaviours.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind and has distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer. This arrangement allows it to detect looming stimuli, and its activity elicits a jump escape response. The LPLC2 visual neuron type has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B of the lobula, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. It projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, and they are cholinergic. VFB holds records of images, splits, neurons with synaptic terminals, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression for LPLC2, but these have not been queried in this session.

results.title: Comparative anatomy
results.question: How does the organisation of the antennal lobe compare between adult and larval Drosophila?
results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") compares between adult and larval Drosophila in terms of glomerular organization, with the adult having approximately 50 glomeruli and the larval having around 22 glomeruli.

results.title: Publications for a circuit
results.question: What publications describe the PPL1 dopaminergic neurons and their role in aversive memory?
results.response: Publications describing the dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and their role in aversive memory include Claridge-Chang et al., 2009, Mao and Davis, 2009, Budnik and White, 1988, and Ren et al., 2016. The dopaminergic PPL1 neurons are located in the posterior inferior lateral protocerebrum of the adult brain and project to various parts of the mushroom body.

VFB also holds [229](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003679,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in fan-shaped body") neuron types with a part in fan-shaped body. results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response: The anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure is: DA1 glomerulus -> adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. VFB does not currently hold Subclasses of [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.response: The neuron types connecting the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") to the [lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00050314 "Open lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018 in Virtual Fly Brain") are PFL1, PFL2_PB4, PFL3_PB7, PFL1_PB1, PFL1_PB7, PFL1_PB2. VFB does not currently hold data on the strength of these connections. VFB does not currently hold data on neurons with presynaptic or postsynaptic terminals in the embryonic/larval lateral accessory lobe.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. It is a [primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047097 "Open primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") with a specific anatomy and connectivity. 

The giant fiber neuron has downstream connectivity classes for DNp01, with [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") results, and upstream connectivity classes for DNp01, with [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") results. 

For transgene expression in DNp01, there are [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") results, including expression patterns for various GAL4 lines such as P{GMR78G07-GAL4}, P{GMR79D08-GAL4}, and P{GMR91H05-GAL4}, as well as intersectional expression patterns like P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} and P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}. 

The giant fiber neuron's connectivity partners include [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047096 "Open secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch OFF hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049540 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [mesothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001985 "Open mesothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), primary neuron, [Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049542 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [prothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001984 "Open prothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049539 "Open Notch ON hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB2-4 lineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048927 "Open NB2-4 lineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049541 "Open Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). 

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Allen et al. (1998), Dorkenwald et al. (2024), and Schlegel et al. (2024).

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response:
Based on connectivity data, neuron types that might mediate a connection between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") include projection neurons and visual projection neurons. Adult visual projection neurons mediate the connection between the visual system and the mushroom body, with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. Other neuron types that might mediate this connection include interneurons, sensory system neurons, secondary neurons, GABAergic neurons, adult GABAergic neurons, input/output neurons, and adult visual projection neurons. 

The mushroom body receives synaptic terminals from [601](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons, according to the "Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body" query. VFB holds scRNAseq data for [visual system neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047736 "Open visual system neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), but this query has not been run yet.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response:
The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is supported by VFB evidence, which suggests a plausible thermosensory influence on mushroom-body memory circuitry through thermosensory projection neurons. VFB records show that thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers, and connectivity between thermosensory neurons and mushroom body is indicated. 

VFB holds [27619](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") images of neurons with some part in mushroom body, but this query has not been run yet. 

Temperature information could influence memory formation, given the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body. VFB has annotated [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body and [304](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body.

results.title: Data availability survey
results.question: I'm interested in studying the subesophageal zone (SEZ). How well-characterised is this region in VFB? What neuron types are annotated, what connectomics data is available, and what genetic tools exist for SEZ neurons?
results.response: The [subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051068 "Open subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") is characterised in VFB with available imagery and various query options for neuron types, parts, subclasses, and transgene expression. VFB holds [2698](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051068,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in subesophageal zone") records of neurons with some part in the subesophageal zone, including [serotonergic SE1 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001980 "Open serotonergic SE1 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [serotonergic SE3 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001982 "Open serotonergic SE3 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [larval CCAP subesophageal IN-1 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111345 "Open larval CCAP subesophageal IN-1 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). There are [4205](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051068,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in subesophageal zone") genetic tools for subesophageal zone neurons, including GAL4 drivers and binary/intersectional drivers, such as [P{GMR12D05-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0057511 "Open P{GMR12D05-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain") and [P{GMR16C05-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0057869 "Open P{GMR16C05-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"). The subesophageal zone has [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051068,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of subesophageal zone") subclasses: [larval subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051067 "Open larval subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") and [adult subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110639 "Open adult subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain"). One image of the subesophageal zone is available, which is the adult subesophageal zone on the adult brain template JFRC2.

results.response:
To cite Virtual Fly Brain in a publication, use the following citation formats:

```

year = {2023},
month = {jan},
abstract = "{As a model organism, Drosophila is uniquely placed to contribute to our understanding of how brains control complex behavior. Not only does it have complex adaptive behaviors, but also a uniquely powerful genetic toolkit, increasingly complete dense connectomic maps of the central nervous system and a rapidly growing set of transcriptomic profiles of cell types. But this also poses a challenge: Given the massive amounts of available data, how are researchers to Find, Access, Integrate and Reuse (FAIR) relevant data in order to develop an integrated anatomical and molecular picture of circuits, inform hypothesis generation, and find reagents for experiments to test these hypotheses? The Virtual Fly Brain (virtualflybrain.org) web application & API provide a solution to this problem, using FAIR principles to integrate 3D images of neurons and brain regions, connectomics, transcriptomics and reagent expression data covering the whole CNS in both larva and adult. Users can search for neurons, neuroanatomy and reagents by name, location, or connectivity, via text search, clicking on 3D images, search-by-image, and queries by type (e.g., dopaminergic neuron) or properties (e.g., synaptic input in the antennal lobe). Returned results include cross-registered 3D images that can be explored in linked 2D and 3D browsers or downloaded under open licenses, and extensive descriptions of cell types and regions curated from the literature. These solutions are potentially extensible to cover similar atlasing and data integration challenges in vertebrates.}",
```

results.title: API: REST endpoints
results.question: How can I query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API?
results.response: To query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically, you can use the Owlery API, which provides OWL reasoning services for Virtual Fly Brain's ontologies. The API endpoint is https://owl.virtualflybrain.org/ and it enables Description Logic (DL) queries, SPARQL queries with OWL reasoning, and access to multiple knowledgebases. Alternatively, the SOLR Search API provides fast text search and autocomplete functionality for Virtual Fly Brain entities, datasets, and publications.

results.title: API: integrations
results.question: How do I explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons using Navis or pymaid?
results.response:
To explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons, you can use the following steps:
```
import pymaid
import navis

navis.set_pbars(jupyter=False)
pymaid.set_pbars(jupyter=False)

# Connect to the VFB CATMAID server hosting the FAFB data
rm = pymaid.connect_catmaid(server="https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org/", api_token=None, max_threads=10)

# Find a neuron from its ID (16) -> this is an olfactory projection neuron
n = pymaid.get_neurons(16)

# Plot CatmaidNeuron with navis
navis.plot3d(n, width=1000, connectors=True, c='k')
```
VFB's documentation does not appear to cover Navis. 
VFB's documentation does not appear to cover pymaid.
